login-demo./description: Follow form validation, token caching, retry backoff, and routing after login.
login-demo./sources/ctl.submit/note: Step 1: validateForm(form) checks input; failures return early
login-demo./sources/ctl.auth/note: Step 2: authenticate() handles authentication; failures go to showError()
login-demo./sources/ctl.route/note: Step 3: routeAfterLogin() chooses the destination after authentication
login-demo./sources/ctl.error/note: All failure paths log a warning and return { error } here
login-demo./sources/val.form/note: Check required fields, then call needsCaptcha() to enforce the captcha threshold
login-demo./sources/val.record/note: Call failures.set() to increment the counter after an authentication failure
login-demo./sources/auth.entry/note: On a cache miss, call requestToken(); on failure, call recordFailure()
login-demo./sources/auth.cache/note: Check tokenCache.get(); on a hit, call loadProfile() directly
login-demo./sources/req.loop/note: Call fetch('/api/login') and parse the token on success
login-demo./sources/req.denied/note: 401 and 423 are definitive rejections: stop without retrying
login-demo./sources/req.retry/note: Retry other responses with exponential backoff; return unavailable after three attempts
login-demo./sources/auth.profile/note: Cache the new token and call loadProfile() to read account state
login-demo./sources/route.fn/note: Choose password reset, then onboarding, then redirectTarget()
login-demo./nodes/0/description: Connect local validation, authentication, and routing.
login-demo./nodes/1/description: Check required fields and the captcha threshold after repeated failures.
login-demo./nodes/2/description: Check the token cache, request a token with backoff, and load the profile.
login-demo./nodes/3/description: Reuse the cached token to load the profile.
login-demo./nodes/4/description: POST /api/login, with up to three attempts and backoff.
login-demo./nodes/5/description: Save the token and request account state from /api/me.
login-demo./nodes/6/description: Prioritize password reset, onboarding, and then an internal redirect.
login-demo./walkthrough/0/title: Start with the controller: three guard clauses
login-demo./walkthrough/0/description: Open onSubmit in login-controller.ts. First follow its outline: validateForm → authenticate → routeAfterLogin. Each failed stage returns showError(...) immediately.
login-demo./walkthrough/0/why: Early returns keep failure paths out of the main flow, avoiding three nested if/else blocks.
login-demo./walkthrough/0/skip: showError only logs a warning and wraps { error }; revisit it at the end.
login-demo./walkthrough/0/example: Alice submits a correct password but no captcha after three earlier failed attempts.
login-demo./walkthrough/1/title: Validate input and enforce the captcha threshold
login-demo./walkthrough/1/description: validateForm checks the username, an eight-character minimum password, and a captcha when needsCaptcha(username) is true. It returns undefined on success or a message on failure.
login-demo./walkthrough/1/why: A string | undefined result handles routine form errors without exceptions and gives the caller a message it can display directly.
login-demo./walkthrough/1/watch: The demo stores failures in an in-memory Map, which resets on refresh. A production application needs server-controlled risk state.
login-demo./walkthrough/1/example: Alice's failure count is three, so needsCaptcha returns true and line 7 asks her to enter a captcha.
login-demo./walkthrough/2/title: Where does the failure counter increase?
login-demo./walkthrough/2/description: recordFailure in validate.ts is called across modules by auth-service.ts when authentication fails, rather than by the validation module itself.
login-demo./walkthrough/2/watch: This shared state couples two modules: changing authentication failure handling can also change validation on the next attempt.
login-demo./walkthrough/3/title: Authenticate: check the in-memory token cache
login-demo./walkthrough/3/description: Alice supplies the captcha and passes validation. authenticate checks tokenCache first; a cache hit goes straight to loading the profile.
login-demo./walkthrough/3/why: The cache avoids an extra POST /api/login round trip for repeated authentication within a short period.
login-demo./walkthrough/3/watch: The example indexes the cache only by username. Production authentication must verify credentials before reusing a session.
login-demo./walkthrough/3/example: This is Alice's first successful login, so the cache is empty and requestToken runs next.
login-demo./walkthrough/4/title: Request a token with retry backoff
login-demo./walkthrough/4/description: requestToken makes up to three POST /api/login attempts. A successful response returns a token; 401 or 423 stops immediately. Other responses wait before retrying. The demo does not catch rejected fetch promises.
login-demo./walkthrough/4/why: The string | { reason: string } return type distinguishes success from failure, allowing the caller to narrow it with typeof token !== 'string'.
login-demo./walkthrough/4/skip: delay is a small Promise wrapper around setTimeout.
login-demo./walkthrough/4/example: Alice's password is correct, so the first request returns 200 OK and a token.
login-demo./walkthrough/5/description: An incorrect password (401) or locked account (423) is a definitive rejection. Sending the same request three times will not help.
login-demo./walkthrough/5/why: Retrying an incorrect password wastes time and can quickly increase failure counts enough to lock the account.
login-demo./walkthrough/6/title: How much time does backoff add?
login-demo./walkthrough/6/description: Other responses wait 200 * 2^attempt milliseconds before the next iteration. Three failed attempts return an unavailable result.
login-demo./walkthrough/6/watch: The waits are 400 ms, 800 ms, and an unnecessary 1600 ms after the final failure: a total of 2.8 seconds. Skipping the last wait is a useful improvement.
login-demo./walkthrough/7/title: Cache the token and load the profile
login-demo./walkthrough/7/description: At authenticate lines 16–17, save the new token in tokenCache, then call loadProfile('/api/me') and return the user state to the controller.
login-demo./walkthrough/7/skip: loadProfile is a standard GET request with a Bearer header.
login-demo./walkthrough/7/example: Alice's token is cached, and /api/me returns { mustChangePassword: false, firstLogin: true }.
login-demo./walkthrough/8/title: Choose the next page in priority order
login-demo./walkthrough/8/description: routeAfterLogin in router.ts checks password reset, first-login onboarding, and finally the URL redirect parameter, defaulting to /home.
login-demo./walkthrough/8/why: The order of if-return clauses encodes priority: a required password change comes before onboarding or an ordinary redirect.
login-demo./walkthrough/8/watch: The demo checks target?.startsWith('/') at line 11. A production implementation must also reject protocol-relative paths such as //example.com.
login-demo./walkthrough/8/example: Alice does not need a password reset, but firstLogin is true, so the result is { page: '/onboarding' }.
login-demo./walkthrough/9/title: Finish at the shared error exit
login-demo./walkthrough/9/description: Return to showError at the bottom of login-controller.ts. Local validation and remote authentication failures both end here to log a warning and return an error object.
login-demo./walkthrough/9/why: A single exit gives you one place to add a toast or error reporting later.
login-demo./tour/example: Alice signs in with the correct password after three failed attempts. It is her first login (firstLogin = true).
login-demo./tour/recap: The controller has three stages: validate.ts checks input and captcha requirements; auth-service.ts handles caching, authentication responses, and profile loading; router.ts chooses the destination by priority.
login-demo./tour/exercise: In auth-service.ts line 29, the third and final failed attempt need not wait another 1600 ms. How would you change the loop to remove that delay?

bag-demo./title: Open the inventory and render items
bag-demo./description: Follow the inventory button through panel creation, cached or remote data loading, and item rendering.
bag-demo./sources/panel.open/note: After creating the panel and loading assets, call refreshList()
bag-demo./sources/panel.read/note: Call loadBag(); use loadFallback() for an empty inventory
bag-demo./sources/repo.load/note: Check cache.get('bag'); on a miss, fetch('/api/bag')
bag-demo./sources/repo.fallback/note: An empty fallback data source when no items are returned
bag-demo./sources/panel.refresh/note: First await readItems() to load inventory items
bag-demo./sources/panel.guard/note: Check the panel still exists, then renderItem() for each item and replace its children
bag-demo./nodes/1/description: Create panel DOM, load assets, and refresh the list.
bag-demo./nodes/2/description: Load data, check the panel, and render.
bag-demo./nodes/3/description: Load inventory data, with an empty fallback.
bag-demo./nodes/4/description: Use memory first; request /api/bag on a cache miss.
bag-demo./nodes/5/description: Default data for an empty inventory.
bag-demo./walkthrough/0/description: Start in bindBagButton: the click listener calls openBagPanel() on line 5. Follow that function next.
bag-demo./walkthrough/0/why: void explicitly discards the Promise: the click handler does not need to wait for rendering.
bag-demo./walkthrough/0/example: The player clicks Inventory and enters openBagPanel().
bag-demo./walkthrough/1/title: openBagPanel: create the panel, then refreshList()
bag-demo./walkthrough/1/description: Create div.bag-panel and save it as the module-level panel, then await ensureAssets() and refreshList() in order. Follow refreshList() at line 10 to see data loading.
bag-demo./walkthrough/1/why: Waiting for assets before rendering prevents item text from appearing before the panel background.
bag-demo./walkthrough/1/watch: panel is a module-level singleton. Two rapid clicks overwrite the first panel reference.
bag-demo./walkthrough/1/example: The panel exists, assets are ready, and refreshList() starts.
bag-demo./walkthrough/2/description: At line 18, refreshList waits for readItems() before checking the panel and rendering. Remember this pause and follow readItems() next.
bag-demo./walkthrough/2/skip: Revisit the guard and rendering on lines 19–20 after the data returns, in step 6.
bag-demo./walkthrough/3/description: readItems awaits loadBag() on line 24. It uses loadFallback() only for an empty array. Follow loadBag() in bag-repository.ts.
bag-demo./walkthrough/3/why: The panel does not need to know where data comes from; its only rule is to fall back when empty.
bag-demo./walkthrough/4/title: loadBag: use the cache or request the API
bag-demo./walkthrough/4/description: Check cache.get('bag') first. On a miss, fetch('/api/bag'), cache the result, and return it through readItems to refreshList.
bag-demo./walkthrough/4/why: Keeping the cache in the repository means callers do not need to distinguish memory from network.
bag-demo./walkthrough/4/watch: An empty array is truthy and is cached too. Future calls keep hitting it until invalidate() clears the cache.
bag-demo./walkthrough/4/example: The first request misses the cache and returns two potions. They are cached, then returned through readItems to refreshList.
bag-demo./walkthrough/5/title: Side path: empty inventory uses loadFallback()
bag-demo./walkthrough/5/description: If loadBag() returns an empty array, readItems returns loadFallback() on line 26.
bag-demo./walkthrough/5/skip: The demo fallback returns [] too; a real application might provide placeholder items.
bag-demo./walkthrough/6/title: Back in refreshList: render only if the panel exists
bag-demo./walkthrough/6/description: Resume after the await on line 18. Line 19 checks panel, then line 20 calls renderItem() for each item and replaces all children in one operation.
bag-demo./walkthrough/6/why: The player may close the panel during the await. closeBagPanel sets panel to undefined, so the guard prevents rendering into a removed panel.
bag-demo./walkthrough/6/example: The panel is still open. Two potions become two spans and the opening flow is complete.
bag-demo./tour/example: The player opens Inventory for the first time, and /api/bag returns two potion items.
bag-demo./tour/recap: Click → openBagPanel → refreshList → readItems → loadBag, then return data to refreshList and render if the panel still exists. The button owns the entry, the panel owns lifecycle and rendering, and the repository owns fetching and caching.
bag-demo./tour/exercise: If the player closes the panel before fetch('/api/bag') finishes, will the returned items still be cached? Follow the code to check your answer.
